key_insight: Strain controls iodine-vacancy pair dynamics in CsPbI3: strong isotropic compression favors separation, tension promotes pair-preserving relay hopping, and biaxial compression produces orientation-dependent responses.
engineering_relevance: Strain engineering may help control defect migration and reconfiguration relevant to the structural stability of halide perovskites.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3 under isotropic and biaxial strain.
Analysis of short-time hopping fractions, pair separation, and relay hopping.
Static vacancy-interaction calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential.
evidence_signal: MLMD shows nonmonotonic strain-dependent hopping and orientation-dependent behavior under biaxial compression, while DFT and SevenNet-0 yield repulsive interactions for every examined configuration.
watch_item: Short-time hopping behavior does not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability or device-scale degradation.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
